title: S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Home Price Indices (August 2026 data) — the repeat-sales price index this calendar tracks nowhere, 9:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: S&P Dow Jones Indices' own press release for the June-2026 edition, press.spglobal.com/2026-08-25-S-P-Cotality-Case-Shiller-Index-Reports-Annual-Gain-in-June-2026, fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200), which states the standing schedule verbatim — "The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Indices are published on the last Tuesday of each month at 9:00 am ET" — and whose own realized publication date, 2026-08-25, IS the last Tuesday of August 2026, anchoring the rule against a 2026 print rather than against the note alone. The two-month reporting lag stated in the same release puts August 2026 data on the October edition. Independently reproduced by weekday arithmetic: October 2026's Tuesdays are the 6th, 13th, 20th and 27th, so 2026-10-27 is the last. Filed `estimate` on two counts, neither of which is date doubt: this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no member for an index provider's own standing publication rule (the same taxonomy gap every S&P DJI entry in this calendar records). Checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the nar-metro-home-prices-2026-10-29 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-08, D-51). The gap it fills: this calendar tracks FHFA HPI monthly and NAR's price series, but ZERO Case-Shiller entries, so the most-cited US repeat-sales home-price index is entirely absent. It matters to the proposing event specifically — Case-Shiller lands two days before the NAR quarterly metro print and reads the same quarter's prices, which is one of the reasons that print carries no new national information (Case-Shiller's national index posted +1.5% for June 2026 against NAR's +1.5% y/y Q2 metro national median). Proposed for the edition inside the proposer's own 5-day corridor rather than backfilling the series. Impact `low` and `symbols: []` on the same measured basis as the proposing ledger: no house playbook is macro- or housing-keyed (0 hits re-grepped 2026-09-08), no instrument attaches, and 10-27 is already a dense session carrying FHFA HPI, new home sales, consumer confidence, durable goods and two Treasury auctions. Nothing here licenses an entry; an estimate widens caution rather than triggering action.
